text.paragraph: Eight-month review before the first full ocrelizumab dose: re-baseline brain MRI, blood counts and immunoglobulins, seasonal vaccines, mobility and work. [S]

Ms. Jordan returns ten weeks after her preventive visit, with a re-baseline brain MRI this morning. She has had no new symptoms and no infection since her first doses. Her mammogram in August was normal, and her HPV test was negative. The heat sensitivity eased as the weather cooled. She finished her course of physical therapy and keeps up her home program and pool exercise; she has had no falls since the near-fall in July. She is teaching a full term and gave two public lectures this month, seated at a lectern. She gets up once a night or less. Dr. Watanabe has reviewed the MRI. Her next infusion, the first full 600 mg dose, is booked in two weeks. [S]

list.item:
Active primary progressive multiple sclerosis (G35.B1). Re-baseline brain MRI without gadolinium: no new or enlarging T2 lesions compared with the diagnostic scan. Disability stable at EDSS 6.0 with a steady timed walk. White cells 6.1, lymphocytes 1.5, hemoglobin 13.5 g/dL, platelets 255; IgG 1010 and IgM 72 mg/dL, both normal; ALT 19 and AST 21 U/L; creatinine 0.80 mg/dL. Safe to give the 600 mg dose. [S]
Ocrelizumab 600 mg in two weeks, with premedication.
Influenza and COVID-19 vaccines today, two weeks before the infusion.
Next brain MRI in one year; immunoglobulins and blood count before each dose.
Dr. Watanabe to review in six months.

Spastic gait and fall risk (R26.89). No falls since one near-fall in the July heat; physical therapy completed. [S]
Continue the home program, pool exercise and baclofen 10 mg three times a day.
Scooter assessment remains open to her.

Neurogenic bladder (N31.9). Controlled on mirabegron; blood pressure normal. [S]

Guideline basis: Practice guideline recommendations summary: Disease-modifying therapies for adults with multiple sclerosis (Rae-Grant A, et al.; PMID 29686116) (2018); 2021 MAGNIMS-CMSC-NAIMS consensus recommendations on the use of MRI in patients with multiple sclerosis (Wattjes MP, et al.; PMID 34139157) (2021); Practice guideline update summary: Vaccine-preventable infections and immunization in multiple sclerosis (Farez MF, et al.; PMID 31462584) (2019); OCREVUS (ocrelizumab) injection, prescribing information (2026); Multiple sclerosis in adults: management (NG220) (2022); Accommodation and Compliance: Multiple Sclerosis (2026); Introduction to the Americans with Disabilities Act (2026); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, osteoporosis and depression monographs (2026); Breast Cancer: Screening (2024)
Follow-up: Ocrelizumab 600 mg in two weeks. Review in three months with the PHQ-9, or the same day for new or worsening symptoms lasting more than 24 hours, fever, or a persistent infection. [S]
